rounds.title: Freeze the question before computing
rounds.summary: Six separate proposals defined models, evidence limits and discriminating controls before peer exchange.
rounds.criticism: Resonant peaks, patent grants, program funding and quantum terminology do not specify net energy. Pressure-only capture estimates and scalar residuals omit necessary information.
rounds.decision: Admit fixed-coupling reciprocal conversion, a loaded piezoelectric receiver, one-qubit work, and independent metrology/identifiability controls. Freeze units, boundaries and tests.
rounds.result: Six source-bound reports; complete energy identities and explicit inverse ambiguities; original version scopes recovered. No sweep or hardware trial was claimed in this round.

rounds.title: Build the models and expose misleading comparisons
rounds.summary: Producers implemented their admitted models while independent reviewers froze alternate formulations and fixtures.
rounds.criticism: At fixed drive amplitude, input power varies with load. Maximum output can differ from maximum efficiency. Shared equations alone do not constitute independent authorship.
rounds.decision: Use explicit RMS conventions, external work/loss quadrature, bounded grids, source-off/storage controls and matrix-based quantum reconstruction. Preserve both passing and deliberately wrong cases.
rounds.result: 1,395-cell electromagnetic and 4,941-cell acoustic grids; metrology phase/storage/aliasing controls; quantum state and unitary-search checks; an exact electrical-identifiability family.

rounds.title: Match input power and challenge the inference
rounds.summary: The advisor selected equal-input sweeps and independent reverse verification in response to Round 2 results.
rounds.criticism: Rescaling a drive can violate current, storage, force or voltage constraints. An unexplained residual cannot be assigned to a new source without additional observations.
rounds.decision: Check constraints after rescaling; compare producer implementations with independently frozen matrix formulations; diagnose three raw synthetic cards before revealing their key.
rounds.result: 613 cross-checks of EM/acoustic calculations and rescaling passed; 648 separately authored quantum cases passed; all three selected blind cases met the rubric, including abstention for the missing-input case. No physical surplus was established.

findings.title: Equal-input comparisons change the engineering decision
findings.detail: The revised sweeps normalize model input, then enforce drive and response constraints. Fixed-voltage or fixed-force output rankings answer a different question.
findings.limit: Finite grids and illustrative linear models; efficiencies exclude named upstream hardware.

findings.title: An electrical fit can leave a mechanical scaling ambiguity
findings.detail: The transformation (m,b,k,g) → (am,ab,ak,√a g) leaves the declared electrical impedance unchanged. Calibrated velocity breaks that positive scaling family.
findings.limit: Known electrical parameters, linear reciprocal model, nonzero coupling and specified inputs; not universal system identification.

findings.title: Stored energy and phase error can mimic an energy surplus
findings.detail: Synthetic tests preserve the wrong reading and its correction. A scalar residual also admits hidden inputs and bias; it does not select a unique cause.
findings.limit: Three blind examples are a selected mechanism check, not a reliability benchmark.

findings.title: Coherence changes extractable work at fixed mean energy
findings.detail: The one-qubit calculator contrasts a pure coherent state and its dephased counterpart, using the same energy reference.
findings.limit: Ideal cyclic-unitary bound; restricted controls may extract less. Device preparation and overhead remain unmodeled.

findings.title: An official unit statement required independent checking
findings.detail: The MARRS solicitation’s picobarn/cm² parenthesis differs from the BIPM conversion by 10²⁴. The original text is preserved and excluded from model inputs.
findings.limit: A source-notation inconsistency does not determine reaction performance or refute the cited studies.

findings.title: Joint energy closure and identifiability as an admission rule
findings.detail: Only promote a conversion claim when it survives a matched-input control, independent energy ledger and sufficient calibrated observations.
findings.limit: A project research thesis and protocol synthesis, not a newly proved law or an observed new energy source.
